description: We're engineers working on energy and climate research. Our team is using NISAR radar data to optimize tracking of agricultural land and water use changes.
summary:
SkyMeter is an open web app that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar to read the fields of Saudi Arabia's 60 largest farming regions, field by field (they hold ~88% of the WorldCover cropland and tree cover in all 114 region boxes; the radar passed its quality check in 42 of them, and the 42 with radar results hold ~64% of it); NISAR passes every 12 days, so the record can be refreshed as passes arrive. 

SkyMeter addresses three questions that are only roughly estimated today, not measured: which fields are actually farmed, how much groundwater and pumping energy they use, and how much organic residue they leave, and where biochar plants could be built to turn residue into durable carbon removal. 

The radar rule calibrates itself against the bare desert in every scene, so it scales nationally with no training labels; field outlines come from ESA Sentinel-2, and we check the radar against Sentinel-2 (a consistency check, since Sentinel-2 also outlines the fields) and against official 2024 statistics. 

It matters because Saudi farming draws on non-renewable aquifers, much of the pumping is unmetered, and the national waste inventory rates farm-residue figures as low confidence. SkyMeter adds an independent, field-by-field radar record that can be refreshed every season, giving water, energy and residue planning a measured basis and supporting the Kingdom’s goals for water and food security.
details:
What SkyMeter does

SkyMeter is an interactive web app that turns NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar into a season-by-season record of Saudi Arabia’s farm fields. Across the country’s 60 largest farming regions it outlines fields from ESA Sentinel-2 and reads NISAR HV backscatter on every field. A field counts as farmed in a season when its backscatter stands above a threshold set from the bare desert on the same radar dates, so the rule needs no training labels.

What it finds (2025/26, central estimates)

  • Farmed area: 188,431 ha in winter and 316,815 ha in summer (357,315 ha in all), in the 42 regions where the radar data pass a quality check; moving the threshold by ±1 dB gives 266,412 to 462,115 ha.
  • Irrigation water: 6.11 billion m³ a year (range 3.60 to 9.84), likely an underestimate, against MEWA’s 11.56 billion m³ for all farms in 2024.
  • Pumping electricity: 3.73 TWh a year, about 845 MW added to the June to September grid peak, and 2.58 Mt CO₂ from grid power.
  • Crop residues: 227 kt of wheat straw and 64 kt of palm fronds from the radar-mapped fields, plus modelled manure placed where animals are housed.
  • Hypothetical biochar plants: 48 plants of 50 kt a year could remove about 0.94 Mt CO₂ a year after transport (all-low to all-high 0.32 to 2.24 Mt). This is a technical potential under the Puro.earth 2025 soil model; poultry litter is not credited because its char fails Puro’s H/C eligibility gate.

How SkyMeter works

Regions come from ESA WorldCover, fields from Sentinel-2 seasonal greenness, and the radar threshold from field-sized desert patches in each scene. On the same benchmark, that beats one national raw-backscatter threshold. Water is farmed area times published or derived irrigation depths, divided by pivot efficiency. Energy uses the regional depth to groundwater plus drawdown and pivot pressure. Every factor has a low, central and high value with its source, shown in the app.

How we checked it

Against Sentinel-2, pooled over regions: kappa 0.24 in winter and 0.45 in summer. In summer, 93% of what the radar calls farmed is green in Sentinel-2, and the radar finds 68% of the green area. A 20 m Qassim deep dive reaches kappa 0.39 and 0.56. Results are also compared with GASTAT and MEWA 2024 statistics. We also tested NISAR coherence and soil moisture: in sand deserts, coherence does not separate fields, a useful finding for NISAR users in arid regions.

Why it matters

Saudi farming draws on non-renewable aquifers, much pumping is unmetered, and farm-residue figures are graded low confidence. One radar record supports groundwater accounting, a field-level baseline for MEWA’s perennial-fodder halt from 16 November 2026, summer grid planning, an independent check of wheat area, and the national residue inventory. The approach can be applied to other dryland farming regions where fields sit in bare desert.

Limitations

NISAR has no Saudi scenes from February to mid-June 2026, so winter area is a lower bound. Water is estimated from crop needs, not metered. Pumping energy is likely a lower bound. Manure is modelled from livestock statistics, and the biochar figures are a technical potential, not credits.
dataRefs: NISAR L2 GCOV (geocoded backscatter, HH/HV, 20 m), NASA ASF DAAC, beta and provisional releases, Oct 2025 – Oct 2026
